The method in a minute

  • Read the day (trend vs range) — it picks the rulebook.
  • In a trend, take second entries with-trend near the 21-EMA — wait for the higher low / lower high.
  • Only with a good signal bar and room to the next level. Scalp 4 ticks, hold a runner to a measured move, 8-tick max stop, never widened.
  • In a range, never the original breakout — fade failures and traps.
  • Most of the skill is the trades he doesn't take → see the Skip Catalog.

Tabs: Top Signals (what he talks about most), Nugget Library (searchable, click a card to flip), Skip Catalog (the no-trades), Rules, Contradictions, Ask Mack (forum Q&A), Decision Gym (practice).

The Rules

The stated framework, condensed from the manual and confirmed across the videos.

Chart & tools

  • One chart: 2000-tick ES (or 10k-volume / 5-min). 21-bar EMA the only indicator; plus drawn trend lines and S/R.
  • Daily chart with envelope bands is reference only — not traded.

Read the day first

  • Market does 3 things: trend up, trend down, range. Decide which — it selects the rulebook.
  • Holding outside the overnight H/L → trend rules. Bound inside → range rules.

Entries

  • Second entry preferred: two legs of correction, enter with-trend; count resets on every new extreme.
  • Wait for the higher low / lower high — don't take the first reversal.
  • Entry = stop order 1 tick beyond a good signal bar (real body, close in correct third, not oversized/doji).
  • Require room to scalp out (~4 ticks) to the next S/R, or no trade.
  • Ranges: never the original breakout — fade the failed break or take the breakout-pullback; fade new daily highs/lows.
  • Traps: a 1–2 tick failed break strands traders; enter where they must exit (signal-bar rule waived).

Management — "scalp and run"

  • Min 2 contracts. 1st target 4 ticks; runner to a measured move, exit just in front.
  • Stop max 8 ticks, 1–2 ticks beyond the entry swing; to break-even after the scalp. Never widen a stop.

Process

  • Take 2–5 best setups, hit the daily goal, then stop (sim after). Flat over news; careful first 5 min; stop ~2:30 CT.
  • Grow size, not trade count. Sim-trade until consistently profitable (double a $10k sim account) before live.

Manual vs Videos

The 2017 manual vs the 2025–26 videos, using four labels: Consistent · Video elaboration · Video-only · Apparent contradiction. A 2017-vs-2026 gap can be evolution, not inconsistency — flagged where relevant.

Apparent contradiction
Take every setup vs discretionary skip. Manual (p.60): "cherry-picking your trades will actually lead to a lower winning percentage." In practice he rejects most counted setups — and in the forum ("2ES LH") endorses skipping a trade he marked good. His reconciliation: sim = take everything; live = 1–3 best.
Video-only
"Room to scalp out before the next S/R." His most-repeated live filter (57 skip-instances) — absent from the manual entirely.
Video-only
"Wait for the higher low / lower high." The dominant no-trade reason (106 instances); the manual barely states it.
Video elaboration
Signal-bar quality. Manual says "good signal bar"; videos add specific vetoes — close-in-third, body:range, size cap, no-doji.
Consistent
Second-entry counting, fading failed range breakouts, measured-move targets, sim-first. Manual and videos agree.
Consistent
Ignore the 21-EMA in ranges. Situational rule (EMA guidance applies to trends) — not a contradiction.

Ask Mack — forum Q&A

Answers Mack writes directly, cross-checked against the library. Sample below; the full browsable index of all scraped threads (question · Mack's answer · his charts, zoom/pan) lives locally in forum/<board>/index.html.

2ES LH
Q: Tempted to take a lower-high 2ES but skipped it — uptrend too strong, unclear what price was doing.
Mack: "I like the trade and I think I marked it as a good one, but if you aren't sure, skipping it is the right move."
Contradicts the manual's take-every-setup rule — he sides with discretionary skipping.
Best place to catch a runner
Q: Where should I look to hold runners?
Mack: "All of the best moves will happen at the KEPs, key entry points... In a tight range, just scalp."
Consistent with the library — KEP is his #1 concept (100 nuggets / 65 videos).
2nd entry short today
Q: Struggling to know when to keep shorting after an STT break + new extreme.
Mack: "Any time you are unsure of what prices are doing, there is NO trade."
His catch-all — safe, but a discretion cue, not a mechanical rule (can't be coded).

Decision Gym

Practice reading his setups — coming

Built from your own ES tick data (2021–2026, covers the corpus): each dated review renders the session up to his marked entry bar, hides the future, you call it (long / short / no-trade + grade), then it reveals his call and the outcome. Spaced repetition on his own answer key.

Honest limit: his exact 2000-tick bars aren't reproducible across data feeds, so this trains reading the same day's price action, not tick-exact mark recovery.

Glossary

His shorthand, decoded.

2ES / 2ELSecond entry short / long
STTShort-term trend line
KEPKey entry point — EMA + trend line + S/R confluence
LH / HLLower high / higher low (the reversal confirmation)
signal barThe bar the entry order sits beyond; must pass the quality test
roomTicks of clear air to the next S/R; gates every entry
runnerHeld portion after the 4-tick scalp; targets a measured move
trap1–2 tick failed break that strands traders; prime scalp
measured movePrior leg/range height projected from the break
count resetThe second-entry count restarts on every new swing extreme
green/blue/redHis trade-grade tiers: conservative / aggressive / advanced-risky
